messages:
Dev Patel: pulling a few recent SUPs that keep coming up in the help channel + tickets. want to align w/ DevEx on doc gaps + what snippets should show. 

Priya Shah: top 3 in the last ~2 weeks:
- SUP-18421 streaming tool-call args look truncated mid-stream (customer thinks we’re dropping bytes)
- SUP-18436 structured output sometimes invalid JSON → parse errors
- SUP-18452 TS tool calling type mismatch vs docs snippet

Priya Shah: also got 2 “stream ended early” reports but those were client disconnects + retry confusion.

Owen Phillips: +1. in SUP-18421 the customer logged each `delta` and assumed `arguments` should be valid JSON every chunk. they were doing `JSON.parse(delta.tool_call.arguments)` per event. blew up.

Markus Klein: we see that in Solutions too. folks treat tool args like “JSON mode streaming” but it’s just string fragments. they need to accumulate, then parse once tool call is complete.

Ibrahim Khan: yep. canonical behavior in our examples should be:
- treat tool call `arguments` as an append-only string buffer during streaming
- only validate/parse on tool-call “final” / completed signal
- show defensive handling: if stream ends before completion → retry w/ idempotency key / request replay

Monica Patel: can we paste the relevant SUP links here so we can cross-reference in docs PR? (even just IDs is fine)

Priya Shah: SUP-18421, SUP-18436, SUP-18452. I can drop redacted snippets if helpful.

SupportBot: Internal note: Jira links may be restricted outside Support. Use ticket IDs when sharing cross-team.

Dana Lo: TS mismatch: our old docs snippet shows tool results as `{ role: 'tool', content: ... }` but SDK expects `tool_result` message w/ `tool_call_id` (and in TS the union didn’t accept the old shape). customer copied docs -> compile error.

Dana Lo: we already have a PR in flight to tighten the types + update snippet. but docs needs to match the released SDK version.

Elliot Price: re docs gap: our current “tool calling” page implies arguments are valid JSON at each streamed delta (bad wording). we should explicitly say: streamed tool args may be partial, don’t parse until finished. add a “Known pitfalls” section.

Wei Chen: + include a small code excerpt showing the “buffer then parse” pattern (Python/TS/Go). right now only Python example kinda hints at it.

Owen Phillips: in SUP-18436, the structured output customer was using streaming + trying to parse incrementally too. but ALSO model sometimes emitted trailing commentary after the JSON object. they didn’t use schema validation / strict mode.

Brian Murphy: we should be careful how we claim guarantees:
- “schema-constrained” reduces drift but not perfect across all models
- show robust approach: validate JSON against schema; if invalid → do a single retry w/ stricter system prompt + optionally disable streaming for that turn

Ibrahim Khan: agree. examples should show:
1) request w/ `response_format` / schema
2) read streaming events → assemble final text
3) parse JSON once final
4) validate; if fail → retry (max 1) OR fall back to non-streaming structured call

Dev Patel: for SUP-18421: doc callout + example change should reduce tickets a lot. customer literally wrote “Redwood truncates tool args” but it’s just partial deltas.

Sabrina James: in the refreshed samples I’m adding a tiny “ToolCallAccumulator” helper (language-idiomatic) so copy/paste users don’t footgun:
- map by `tool_call_id`
- append `arguments_delta`
- when `tool_call.completed` (or equivalent) → `JSON.parse(accumulated)`

Sabrina James: and log like `tool_call_partial_args=true` in debug so support can identify instantly.

Dana Lo: for TS, we should also show parallel tool calls (customer confusion: they assumed exactly one tool call). in streaming they may get interleaved deltas for multiple tool_call_ids.

Ibrahim Khan: +1. canonical mental model:
- events are per response
- tool calls are a set, each identified by id
- deltas can arrive interleaved
- consumer must route deltas by id

Wei Chen: can we add explicit “don’t assume order” language + a short diagram-ish list in docs? (no need for actual diagram)

Elliot Price: yup. I’ll add a “Streaming tool calls: assembly rules” section. also add a small snippet for error handling:
- on disconnect: surface partial state, retry request
- on `rate_limited` / `server_error`: backoff

Owen Phillips: small but common: customers forget to send tool results back as a message before asking model to continue. they run the tool locally and then just call `responses.create()` w/ the next user message. model has no idea tool succeeded.

Markus Klein: yep. should show the loop:
1) model requests tool
2) execute tool(s)
3) send `tool_result` messages referencing `tool_call_id`
4) model continues

Monica Patel: action items? trying to map to owners.

Ibrahim Khan: proposals:
- Docs: add “Known pitfalls” bullets referencing SUP-18421/36/52 patterns (Elliot/Wei)
- Examples: ensure each language shows accumulator + parallel tool calls (Sabrina + Dana + Mateusz, etc)
- SDK: TS typing + migration note (Dana)
- Support: macro reply template for “partial tool args” + “structured output invalid JSON” (Priya/Dev)

Priya Shah: I can draft support macros today. include: “If streaming tool-call args: buffer + parse only after complete. If streaming structured output: parse at end, validate, retry once, or disable streaming.”

Dev Patel: also add a one-liner we can paste: “Tool arguments may be partial during streaming; they are not guaranteed to be valid JSON until the tool call is finalized.”

Brian Murphy: also, make sure examples don’t imply “exactly valid JSON always”. we can say “expected to be valid at completion; validate anyway.”

Elliot Price: I’ll thread this into the docs PR. quick list of doc edits:
- correct terminology: “structured output” (not “JSON mode”)
- add “Partial args during streaming” callout with code
- add “Parallel tool calls” callout
- add “Validation + retry” section for structured output

Dana Lo: for TS snippet, we should pin to the SDK minor version in the docs tab header (or at least note “Requires redwood-sdk >= x.y”). otherwise we’ll re-break copy/paste.

Wei Chen: we can add a “Version note” line under code tabs (tiny). also a link to runnable examples repo.

Sabrina James: I’ll make sure the runnable samples print expected console output so support can ask customers “does yours look like this?”

Owen Phillips: :thumbsup: would love that. so many tickets are just “it doesn’t work” without a baseline.

Markus Klein: one more doc gap: OpenAI-compat assumptions. some customers compare payload shapes and get confused by field names. should we add a small note: “If you’re using OpenAI compat, see differences here”?

Ibrahim Khan: yes but keep it short. link out to compat doc. don’t clutter main flow.

Dev Patel: ok. I’ll sync with Priya on macros + add these notes to the support enablement checklist.

Priya Shah: dropping a redacted excerpt from SUP-18421 to illustrate the misunderstanding:
```
stream event: tool_call.delta arguments="{\"q\": \"best "
stream event: tool_call.delta arguments="latency\"" 
// customer does JSON.parse() on each line
```

Brian Murphy: perfect example. we should literally include a tiny “anti-pattern” snippet in docs: “Don’t do this”.

Elliot Price: yes. anti-pattern callout + correct pattern.

Monica Patel: great. Ibrahim can you make sure the parity guidelines mention anti-pattern too? so reviewers catch it.

Ibrahim Khan: will do. I’ll update the checklist: “No incremental JSON.parse on streamed args; buffer and parse on completion.”

Dev Patel: closing loop: target is to see SUP volume drop in 1-2 weeks after publish. we’ll monitor ticket tags.

SupportBot: Reminder: If publishing new docs, add internal note in #support-announcements with links + macros.
